source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-5

procedures.title: Battery and battery cables: service
steps: Measure electrolyte specific gravity in each cell (see figure 6 in the manual); if under 1.230 corrected to 80°F, slow-charge the battery or test it further.

Disconnect the coil primary lead at the negative terminal so the engine cannot fire, then read battery terminal voltage with a voltmeter while cranking; under 9.0 volts at roughly 80° ± 20°F means the battery needs more testing (Section 6Y).
Look for corrosion on the battery, cables and nearby area, loose or broken carriers, cracked or bulged case, dirt and acid, leaking electrolyte and low level.
Top up the cells with distilled or demineralized water.
Keep the battery top clean of acid film and dirt: wash with a weak ammonia or soda solution to neutralize acid, then rinse with clean water, keeping the vent plugs tight so solution cannot get in.
Tighten the hold-down bolts enough to stop the battery moving, but not so much that the case is strained.
Make sure the cables are tight on the posts; oil the terminal felt washer.
Clean corroded posts and cable terminals separately with soda solution and a wire brush, then coat posts and clamps thinly with petrolatum before refitting.

specs.what: minimum cranking terminal voltage at about 80° ± 20°F

notes: A battery that stays undercharged points to a loose or bad fan belt, defective Delcotron, high charging-circuit resistance, oxidized regulator points or a low voltage setting.
A battery using too much water means voltage output is too high.

procedures.title: Delcotron and regulator: tune-up check
steps: Use the battery checks above as the tune-up test of the charging system; follow up per Section 6Y as the battery condition indicates.

procedures.title: Drive belts: service
steps: Measure tension with a strand tension gauge (see figure 7 in the manual).
Adjust to the tension given in the Tune Up Chart.

procedures.title: Manifold heat control valve: service
steps: Check that the valve moves freely (see figure 9 in the manual for the V8).
Free a sticking shaft with GM Manifold Heat Control Solvent or equivalent, tapping the shaft end to end to help loosen it.

procedures.title: Intake manifold: tighten
steps: Torque the intake manifold bolts to specifications in the order on the Torque Sequence Chart.
notes: Even a small intake manifold leak ruins performance and economy.
